requested.title: Revoked relay instances continue receiving webhook payloads

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The administrator-only DELETE route correctly requires an authenticated admin and then calls revokeRelayInstance, but that function only updates forge_relay_instances.status to "revoked" and sets revoked_at. It neither removes installation claims/link mirrors nor marks pending forge_relay_deliveries terminal, and the database schema has no status-dependent cascade or policy that would do so. For GitHub, enqueueRelayDeliveryForPayload resolves an incoming, signature-verified delivery solely through forge_relay_installations.instance_id and inserts a pending delivery without joining or filtering forge_relay_instances by active status. For GitLab, the public relay webhook similarly authorizes against the retained link-mirror webhook secret and enqueues to its instance_id without an active-instance check. The cron worker selects pending rows and joins only webhook_url and webhook_secret_encrypted; a revoked instance with its previously registered endpoint and secret is therefore still POSTed the signed raw payload. Relay request signing does reject a revoked instance from making subsequent control-plane calls, and cron authentication protects who can invoke the worker, but neither mitigation constrains this outbound delivery path. A concrete scenario is an instance compromise followed by an administrator revocation: later provider webhooks for its still-claimed installation or mirrored GitLab repository, plus already queued rows, continue to reach the attacker-controlled registered endpoint. This contradicts both the route documentation and the managed-forge design requirement that revocation immediately stops webhook fan-out, so the HIGH severity is appropriate.
